messages:
zara: quick heads-up: eu-west dedicated pool (rack-eu3) p95/p99 jitter started at 07:14 UTC. TL;DR: noisy tenant + SR-IOV VF steering bounce. noticed VF rebinds coincide with tail latency.

zara: gathered a couple logs, output below. looks like Flow Director rules thrash when several high-concurrency flows hit same VF.

zara: ```
# ethtool -S enp1s0f0 | egrep 'vf|rx_'
vf_rx: 0
vf_tx: 0
queue0_rx: 8900000
queue1_rx: 420000
queue2_rx: 12000
queue3_rx: 35000
# tc -s qdisc show dev enp1s0f0
qdisc fq_codel 0: root backlog 0p requeues 0 tx_packets 200012 tx_bytes 120003210
```

zara: also dmesg shows firmware warnings around VF reset: "mlx5_core: VF 2 rebind due to flow_dir update" on a couple hosts.

otto: hmm. sounds like Flow Director + VF mapping oscillation. Which tenant ids?

zara: main offender is tenant=nlp-parallel, plus some background batch jobs from tenant=batch-ml. nlp-parallel opens many short-lived connections (tens of reqs/s per pod) and we see PF/VF rule churn.

mei: options: 1) quick: apply per-tenant tc ingress policer + reduce conn burst (token bucket), 2) moderate: pin nlp-parallel pods to a different VF / physical NIC via SR-IOV mapping, 3) heavy: ephemeral fractional dedicated slice (0.2) + dedicated NIC carveout. Each has ops/cost tradeoffs.

ryan: for (2) we can change vf-bind scheduling and add a flow carve (Flow Director rule) to map their 5-tuples to VF3 persistently, avoid churn. Risk: if the VF gets hot it still impacts others on same NIC.

zara: I tried a quick tc ingress limit on one host: `tc filter add dev enp1s0f0 protocol ip parent 1:0 u32 match ip src 10.10.0.0/16 police rate 150mbit burst 10kb drop flowid :1` — initial results look promising. p95 down from ~380ms -> ~160ms, p99 from 1.1s -> 460ms.

ops-bot: Action: ingress-policer rule rp-227 applied to tenant=nlp-parallel on hosts [eu3-node7, eu3-node8]. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ingress-policer

otto: good quick win. but this is a symptom; flow_dir firmware churn suggests a buggy NIC driver/firmware combo. Any recent firmware mismatches in eu3?

mei: eu3 had mixed NIC fw: some nodes on mlx5fw 22.11, others on 22.8. we'll need a coordinated firmware homogenization. that should reduce rule-regen mismatch. schedule during next maintenance window.

ryan: Meanwhile, for customers we should prepare two offers: burst-protection (soft isolation + policer + premium per-GB for excess) and ephemeral carveout (0.2 slice, 2-6h) with warm-pool prefetch to avoid kv-cache cold penalty. Provide cost delta to account team.

billing-bot: Rough estimate: ephemeral 0.2 GPU-slice in eu-west for 4h prorated = approx +25% marginal infra charge for that workload. Burst-protection premium: +2x egress surcharge for bytes above threshold or per-minute burst fee. Ping me with tenant id for exact numbers.

zara: plan for next 30m: keep ingress policer rp-227 active, add persistent Flow Director carve for known 5-tuples (pinning) on affected hosts, and open INF ticket to track firmware homogenization. If p99 doesn't drop below 500ms, propose ephemeral carveout.

otto: add SLO board note. if this repeats across racks we escalate to regional mitigations (move some tenants to alternate AZ).

mei: pinned FD carve for nlp-parallel on eu3-node7/8. applied rule fd-99. monitoring.

zara: 10m after policer+FD: p95 -> 140ms, p99 -> 420ms. Improvement but still occasional tails during burst windows. Keeping policy + pin for now.

ryan: thanks. can someone file the cost/impact calc and tag billing + account? include kv-cache warmup notes (first ~5-15s may be slower when we carveout due to prefix prefetch).

zara: filing INF-6234 with perf graphs and tcpdump. tagging @billing-bot & @account-eng.

ops-bot: Reminder: paste final timeline + mitigations into INF-6234 when resolved. :memo:

zara: will follow up after the maintenance window and share firmware rollout plan. thx all. :thumbsup:
